items.stem: What is meant by market equilibrium?
options: A situation where price is set by the government
A situation where all firms make a profit
A situation where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied and there is no tendency for price to change
A situation where demand is greater than supply
items.answer: A situation where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied and there is no tendency for price to change
items.markingKey: Equilibrium: market clears.

items.stem: Explain how a market moves to equilibrium if the price is initially above the equilibrium level.
items.answer: There is excess supply: unsold stocks build up, so sellers cut prices; as price falls quantity demanded extends and quantity supplied contracts until they are equal.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: excess supply; 1 mark: price falls; 1 mark: extensions/contractions to equilibrium [3]

items.stem: Explain why equilibrium is described as a position of rest.
items.answer: At equilibrium buyers can buy all they want and sellers can sell all they want at that price, so there is no pressure for price to change unless conditions change.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: market clears; 1 mark: no pressure to change [2]

items.stem: The market for fresh fruit in Ostrelia is described by Qd = 180 − 4P and Qs = 30 + 6P, where Q is in thousands of units a week and P in dollars. Calculate the equilibrium price.

The market for concert tickets in Tarvia is described by Qd = 190 − 10P and Qs = 10 + 2P, where Q is in thousands of units a week and P in dollars. (a) Calculate the equilibrium price and quantity. (b) Calculate the shortage if the price were $9. (c) Explain how the market would return to equilibrium.
items.answer: (a) P = $15, Q = 40 thousand. (b) At $9: Qd = 100, Qs = 28: excess demand of 72 thousand. (c) Price rises; Qd contracts and Qs extends until equal.
items.markingKey: (a) solve 190 − 10P = 10 + 2P [1]; P and Q [1] (b) Qd and Qs at $9 [1]; difference [1] (c) adjustment process [1] [5]

items.stem: The market for streaming subscriptions in Sundara is described by Qd = 136 − 3P and Qs = 28 + 6P, where Q is in thousands of units a week and P in dollars. (a) Calculate the equilibrium price and quantity. (b) Calculate the shortage if the price were $8. (c) Explain how the market would return to equilibrium.
items.answer: (a) P = $12, Q = 100 thousand. (b) At $8: Qd = 112, Qs = 76: excess demand of 36 thousand. (c) Price rises; Qd contracts and Qs extends until equal.
items.markingKey: (a) solve 136 − 3P = 28 + 6P [1]; P and Q [1] (b) Qd and Qs at $8 [1]; difference [1] (c) adjustment process [1] [5]

A popular social media campaign has increased demand by 14 thousand units at every price. Producers say they cannot increase output quickly because of a shortage of skilled workers. (a) Calculate the original equilibrium price and quantity. (b) Calculate the new equilibrium price and quantity.

Extract: The market for restaurant meals in Westaria can be represented by Qd = 160 − 2P and Qs = 20 + 5P (Q in thousands per month, P in dollars). A popular social media campaign has increased demand by 7 thousand units at every price. Producers say they cannot increase output quickly because of a shortage of skilled workers. (a) Calculate the original equilibrium price and quantity. (b) Calculate the excess demand at the original price after the campaign. (c) Calculate the new equilibrium price and quantity.
If the market price is above the equilibrium price, there will be
options: excess supply, putting downward pressure on price
items.answer: excess supply, putting downward pressure on price
items.markingKey: Surplus → price falls.

items.stem: Extract: The market for smartphones in Marvona can be represented by Qd = 130 − 4P and Qs = −10 + 3P (Q in thousands per month, P in dollars). A popular social media campaign has increased demand by 7 thousand units at every price. Producers say they cannot increase output quickly because of a shortage of skilled workers. (a) Calculate the new equilibrium price and quantity. (b) Discuss whether the shortage of skilled workers means the price rise will be large and long-lasting.
items.answer: (a) P = $21, Q = 53 (b) Inelastic supply → large price rise in short run; in long run training, migration, technology and entry raise supply; campaign may be a fad; judgement.
items.markingKey: (a) 137 − 4P = −10 + 3P [2] (b) Credit: Inelastic supply → large price rise in short run; in long run training, migration, technology and entry raise supply; campaign may be a fad; judgement. [4]

items.stem: What happens to equilibrium price and quantity when demand increases and supply is unchanged?
items.answer: Both rise
items.markingKey: Demand shifts right along an upward-sloping supply curve.

items.stem: Explain, using demand and supply analysis, the effect of an increase in costs of production on a market.
items.answer: Supply shifts left: at the original price there is excess demand, so price rises; quantity demanded contracts until the new equilibrium has a higher price and lower quantity.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: supply shifts left; 1 mark: excess demand/price rises; 1 mark: new equilibrium higher P lower Q [3]

items.stem: Explain why the effect on equilibrium price is uncertain when demand and supply both increase.
items.answer: The demand increase pushes price up while the supply increase pushes it down; the net effect depends on which shift is larger.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: opposing pressures; 1 mark: depends on relative size [2]

items.stem: Incomes fall and consumers see concert tickets as a normal good. What is the likely effect on the equilibrium price and quantity in the market?
items.answer: Price falls, quantity falls
items.markingKey: Price falls, quantity falls: demand shifts left.

items.stem: A popular film increases the fashion for cement. What is the likely effect on the equilibrium price and quantity in the market? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Price rises, quantity rises: demand shifts right.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Price rises, quantity rises; 1 mark: explanation – demand shifts right. [2]

items.stem: For each event, state the effect on equilibrium price and quantity and explain why. (i) The population of Dhaka increases rapidly, raising demand for housing. (ii) Incomes fall and consumers see printed newspapers as a normal good.
items.answer: (i) Price rises, quantity rises (ii) Price falls, quantity falls
items.markingKey: (i) Price rises, quantity rises – demand shifts right. [2] (ii) Price falls, quantity falls – demand shifts left. [2] Total [4]

items.markingKey: 1 mark: both shifts; 1 mark: Q rises, P indeterminate [2]

items.stem: What is meant by derived demand?
options: Demand that comes from the government
Demand for a good or factor that arises from the demand for another product
Demand that is unrelated to price
items.answer: Demand for a good or factor that arises from the demand for another product
items.markingKey: e.g. labour, raw materials.

items.stem: Explain, with an example, how a change in the market for one good can affect the market for a good in joint supply.
items.answer: More cattle are slaughtered when demand for beef rises, so the supply of leather increases; leather’s price falls and quantity rises.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: example; 1 mark: supply shift; 1 mark: price/quantity effect [3]

items.stem: Explain why the demand for labour is described as a derived demand.
items.answer: Firms hire workers not for their own sake but to produce goods and services that consumers demand; if demand for the product falls, demand for labour falls.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: definition; 1 mark: link to product demand [2]

items.stem: Tea and coffee. Which relationship between markets does this illustrate?
items.answer: Competitive demand
items.markingKey: Competitive demand: substitutes.

items.stem: Tea and coffee. Which relationship between markets does this illustrate? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Competitive demand: substitutes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Competitive demand; 1 mark: explanation – substitutes. [2]

items.stem: Extract: The market for printed newspapers in Calvania can be represented by Qd = 280 − 10P and Qs = 40 + 2P (Q in thousands per month, P in dollars). A popular social media campaign has increased demand by 12 thousand units at every price. Producers say they cannot increase output quickly because of a shortage of skilled workers. (a) Calculate the original equilibrium price and quantity. (b) Calculate the new equilibrium price and quantity.
Explain how composite demand can cause the price of a good to rise.
items.answer: If demand for one use rises (e.g. milk for cheese), less is available for other uses at the original price, so the overall price rises and other users pay more.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: competing uses; 1 mark: price effect [2]

items.stem: In Merania, the number of cattle slaughtered for beef rose from 400 thousand to 500 thousand a year after demand for beef increased. Each animal provides one hide used for leather. Calculate the percentage increase in the supply of hides.
Which function of the price mechanism allocates scarce goods to those most willing and able to pay?
items.answer: Rationing
items.markingKey: Higher prices ration limited supply.

items.stem: Explain the signalling, incentive and rationing functions of the price mechanism.
items.answer: Signalling: price changes convey information about demand and supply. Incentive: higher prices/profits encourage producers to supply more (and consumers to buy less). Rationing: price allocates scarce goods to those willing and able to pay.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each function [3]

items.stem: Explain how the price mechanism responds to an increase in demand for a product.
items.answer: Price rises (signal); higher profits attract resources (incentive), raising supply; the higher price rations the good among buyers until a new equilibrium.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each stage [3]

items.stem: A rise in the price of smartphones tells producers that consumers want more of it. Which function of the price mechanism does this illustrate?
items.answer: Signalling function
items.markingKey: Signalling function: price changes convey information to producers and consumers.

items.stem: A fall in the price of chocolate bars tells firms to reduce output and move resources elsewhere. Which function of the price mechanism does this illustrate? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Signalling function: information about changing demand.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Signalling function; 1 mark: explanation – information about changing demand. [2]

items.stem: Extract: The market for bottled water in Halvoria can be represented by Qd = 80 − 3P and Qs = 10 + 4P (Q in thousands per month, P in dollars). A popular social media campaign has increased demand by 7 thousand units at every price. Producers say they cannot increase output quickly because of a shortage of skilled workers. (a) Calculate the original equilibrium price and quantity. (b) Calculate the new equilibrium price and quantity.
Hotel rooms in Nairobi during a festival go to those willing to pay the highest prices. Which function of the price mechanism does this illustrate?
items.answer: Rationing function
items.markingKey: Rationing function: price allocates a limited number of rooms.

items.stem: If the market price is below the equilibrium price, there will be
options: excess demand, putting upward pressure on price
items.answer: excess demand, putting upward pressure on price
items.markingKey: Shortage → price rises.

items.stem: Unsold stocks of televisions are piling up in warehouses in Istrana. Explain what will happen to the price in a free market.
items.answer: Excess supply: firms cut prices to sell stocks; quantity demanded extends and quantity supplied contracts until equilibrium.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: excess supply; 1 mark: price falls to equilibrium [2]

items.stem: Tickets for a concert in Cape Town sold out in minutes and were resold online at three times the original price. Explain what this shows about the original price.
items.answer: It was below equilibrium: excess demand meant some buyers were willing to pay much more, creating a secondary market.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: below equilibrium/excess demand; 1 mark: resale price evidence [2]

items.stem: The market for gym memberships in Selmaria is described by Qd = 120 − 4P and Qs = −30 + 6P, where Q is in thousands of units a week and P in dollars. Calculate the equilibrium price.

(b) Calculate the shortage if the price were $2. (c) Explain how the market would return to equilibrium.
items.answer: (a) P = $4, Q = 60 thousand. (b) At $2: Qd = 80, Qs = 40: excess demand of 40 thousand. (c) Price rises; Qd contracts and Qs extends until equal.
items.markingKey: (a) solve 100 − 10P = 20 + 10P [1]; P and Q [1] (b) Qd and Qs at $2 [1]; difference [1] (c) adjustment process [1] [5]

items.stem: A policy institute in Lisbon has published a report on this issue for the government of Valdoria. Assess whether markets in Valdoria will always move quickly to equilibrium.
items.answer: For: Price flexibility clears markets; competition; information via prices. Against: Sticky prices, contracts, government controls, inelastic supply, information failures, speculation; disequilibrium can persist (housing, labour markets). Conclusion: a reasoned judgement on when the claim holds.
items.markingKey: Analysis (AO1/AO2, up to 8): Price flexibility clears markets; competition; information via prices. Evaluation (AO3, up to 4): Sticky prices, contracts, government controls, inelastic supply, information failures, speculation; disequilibrium can persist (housing, labour markets). Top marks need balanced analysis of both sides and a justified conclusion that answers the question set, explaining what the outcome depends on [12]

items.stem: What happens to equilibrium price and quantity when supply increases and demand is unchanged?
items.answer: Price falls and quantity rises
items.markingKey: Supply shifts right along a downward-sloping demand curve.

items.stem: A student, Samuel, claims: ‘If demand and supply both increase, the equilibrium price must rise.’ Identify what is wrong with this reasoning and give the correct explanation.
items.answer: Quantity must rise, but price may rise, fall or stay the same depending on the relative size of the shifts.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error; 1 mark: correct explanation – Quantity must rise, but price may rise, fall or stay the same depending on the relative size of the shifts. [2]

items.stem: In the market for bus journeys, Qd = 140 − 4P and Qs = −70 + 10P (Q in thousands, P in dollars). After a successful advertising campaign, the demand equation becomes Qd = 182 − 4P. Calculate the new equilibrium price.
A storm destroys much of the Kestria banana crop. What is the likely effect on the equilibrium price and quantity in the market?
items.answer: Price rises, quantity falls
items.markingKey: Price rises, quantity falls: supply shifts left.

items.stem: In the market for cinema tickets, Qd = 132 − 4P and Qs = 52 + 6P (Q in thousands, P in dollars). After a fall in raw material costs, the supply equation becomes Qs = 62 + 6P. (a) Calculate the equilibrium price and quantity before and after the change. (b) Explain the process by which the market reaches the new equilibrium.
items.answer: (a) Before: P = $8, Q = 100; after: P = $7, Q = 104. (b) Supply shifts right: excess supply at the old price pushes price down; demand extends.
items.markingKey: (a) old equilibrium [1]; new equilibrium [2] (b) shift, disequilibrium and adjustment [2] [5]

items.stem: What is meant by joint supply?
options: Two firms supplying the same market
Production of one good automatically leads to production of another
items.answer: Production of one good automatically leads to production of another
items.markingKey: By-products: beef/leather.

items.stem: A boom in house building in Korvia raises demand for bricks and cement. Explain the type of demand involved and its effect on the market for cement.
items.answer: Derived demand: demand for cement comes from demand for houses; it shifts right, raising price and quantity of cement.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: derived; 1 mark: market effect [2]

items.stem: Cars and petrol. Which relationship between markets does this illustrate?
items.answer: Joint demand
items.markingKey: Joint demand: the goods are complements used together.

items.stem: Hana, an economics student in Muscat, is preparing for a class debate on this topic. Explain, with examples, the difference between joint demand, competitive demand, derived demand, composite demand and joint supply.

items.stem: Explain one limitation of using price to allocate places at popular schools in Jovania.
items.answer: Places would go to the richest families, not those with the most need or ability; inequity and lost potential.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: rationing by ability to pay; 1 mark: inequity/inefficiency [2]

items.stem: Demand for electric bicycles in Cairo has doubled. Explain how the price mechanism will respond.
items.answer: Price rises, signalling higher demand; profits rise, giving an incentive to increase supply and enter the market; the higher price rations bikes until supply catches up.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: signal; 1 mark: incentive; 1 mark: rationing [3]

items.answer: Signalling, incentive and rationing; reallocation between markets; example of a demand increase.

items.stem: Lina wrote in a homework answer: ‘At equilibrium, demand and supply are both at their maximum.’ Explain what is wrong with this claim.
items.answer: At equilibrium the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied at the market price; neither is at a maximum.
